name: Thai Sign Language
sweep_summary: Thai Sign Language (thai1240) is not in the catalog, and both sweep items are Glottolog misattributions: Glottolog 5.1 hangs Tumtavitikul 1998 (SEALS IV, listed as 'Warotamasikkhadit and Panakul 1997', ref 684097) and Potisuk, Gandour & Harper 1994 (LTBA 17.2, ref 177821) on thai1240 because their titles say 'Thai', but both are about spoken Standard/Bangkok Thai (thai1261), where Glottolog also lists the same works (8693, 8686, 675826) and our already holds Potisuk 1994. I fetched sources the full SEALang SALA scan of Tumtavitikul 1998 (20 pp, scanned at 300 dpi; and read its stress section: for spoken Thai, primary stress is always word-final, non-final syllables are stressed by weight, derived by right-headed leftward unbounded feet (pp. 63-65). Potisuk 1994 (same file already on file under thai1261, byte-identical) is an acoustic study of Bangkok Thai compound stress. Neither says anything about a sign language, so no first-hand stress statement for Thai Sign Language was found (best_new_statement found=false). Crossref title searches for 'Thai Sign Language' (40 rows) and 'Thai Sign Language prosody/stress' (14 rows) returned nothing on prosody or stress in TSL; the Glottolog thai1240 page cites no phonology work. Recommended action: re-point Glottolog 684097 and 177821 to thai1261 in our per-language bibliography; the scanned Tumtavitikul 1998 text is now available for the spoken-Thai sweep. written in the thai1240 folder.
